_readme: Config for the contract_br provisioning depth: which BR rule-value-mapping bodies to
create so a CONTRACT (rather than an apiKey) drives the markup rules.
Each item under 'conditions' is POSTed to /rulevaluemappings verbatim, except
inputValue, which SMF fills in from the contracts it just created.
contract_value_field : which contract attribute becomes inputValue. 'autoId' is the
short numeric id the real 'contractId IN' condition matches
(e.g. 10103) — SMF reads it back from Backoffice after
creating each contract. 'uid' and 'id' (mongo _id) are also
available.
value_mode           : 'join' (default) puts every contract in ONE condition as a
separated list, which is what operator IN expects.
'per_contract' creates one condition per contract instead,
for a single-value operator such as EQUALS.
value_separator      : default ','.
The stg body below came from a working request against STAGING. inputDetailId 30 is
'contractId IN' (field contractId, operator IN, datatype STRING) and the condition
hangs under the 'apikey IN' parent (id 5) of rule 3 (Static Markup).
dev is {} because these ids are ENVIRONMENT data — the parent condition id in
particular. Do not copy the stg block to dev without checking the ids there; a wrong
parent id makes the BR step fail loudly rather than silently.
To add Dynamic Markup (rule 4), append a second entry with ruleId '4' and that
rule's own 'apikey IN' parent id. inputDetailId stays 30 (the input field is the
same); only the rule and its parent change.
To disable for an env, set it to {} — contract_br then still creates the mocks and
contract and reports the BR step as NOT_CONFIGURED.
